newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Hyder yr profits, gearing to rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hyder yr profits, gearing to rise.

text.p: British multi-utility Hyder Plc should show a strong gain in year profits when it reports on June 9 as its takeover of South Wales Electricity (Swalec) bears fruit, but gearing could suffer, analysts said.
"The full-year impact of Swalec should be earnings enhancing but gearing could be high. How high will certainly be of interest," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Hyder took over its local regional electricity company (Rec) Swalec at the beginning of 1996 and said in November that the acquisition should be earnings enhancing on a full-year basis.

Pre-tax profits for the group are expected to rise strongly to between 206.3 and 212 million stg from 167.9 million previously and a dividend payout of around 44.0-44.4 pence per share is expected, up from 38.7 pence.
Analysts said there would also be interest in any updates on cost savings from the merged group and more details on the proforma results of its individual business arms.
"It would be nice to see more how these multi-utilities are shaping up," the analyst said.
Hyder stands with United Utilities and Scottish Power as the country's three multi-tasking utility companies spanning water, electricity and other areas such as gas and telecommunications.
But political issues are also likely to focus the market's attention at results, analysts said.
"We have not heard much on the government's planned tax or on extra capital spending needed to meet tighter targets on cutting leaks," the analyst said.

The new Labour government, swept to power in a landslide victory on May 1, has made a one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities a central plank of its first budget, scheduled for July 2.
It has also vowed to introduce mandatory targets for cutting leaks as nearly 800 million gallons seep out of pipes daily while the country struggles with its worst drought in 200 years.

Companies have submitted comments to the Treasury on the so-called "windfall" tax and were given three weeks in mid-May to submit plans to meet leakage targets and other issues in a 10-point plan drawn up to tackle the drought by the government.
Hyder has already recognised that it will have to pay any windfall tax and analysts will be looking for any indications on amounts.

"These are the really crucial issues. Shares are undervalued because of them at the moment so there is not much room for the share price to move if there is any profit fall, which shows that isn't important," the analyst said.
Hyder shares were standing at 817.5 pence by 1215 GMT, up 8.5 pence but well off a year high of 864 pence.
